claims.text: The nanoparticles are initially solid before examination.
Chemical complexity governs the premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Varied nanoscale configurations govern the premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Nanoscale phase-transition behavior governs the premelting and melting response of these nanoparticles.
In situ X-ray powder diffraction and multi-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy can elucidate the proposed governing interplay.
Laser solid-phase synthesis is the intervention used to prepare the nanoparticles.
The high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will exhibit a thermal response distinct from single-metal nanoparticles.
The high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will exhibit a thermal response distinct from bimetallic nanoparticles.
The hypothesis applies within cooling-rate and temperature ranges that consolidate the solid solution.
A thermal and phase-transition response identical to that of single-metal or bimetallic nanoparticles would falsify the hypothesis.
